title: Adjectives
objectives: understand English adjectives and their various uses
learn and translate various Greek adjectives
identify attributive, predicate, and substantive uses of Greek adjectives
properly identify the grammatical agreement between an adjective and its accompanying substantive
identify the various forms of the verb εἰμί in the present active indicative
master 10 more high frequency vocabulary words

content.text: An adjective is a word used to modify a noun or pronoun. The adjective often specifies more clearly what the noun or pronoun actually means. It often answers the question "What kind of ______ is it?"

The [[u]]soft[[/u]] snow hit the windshield.
    Answers:  what kind of snow?  soft
The snow was [[u]]soft[[/u]].

items.label: Attributive:
items.text: the adjective attributes a characteristic to the noun it modifies.

items.label: Predicate:
items.text: the adjective assigns a characteristic to the subject of the sentence.

items.label: Substantive:
items.text: the adjective acts independently as a noun itself.

items.label: Attributive use:
exampleLines: The [[u]]red[[/u]] car hit the [[u]]big[[/u]] truck behind the [[u]]rear[[/u]] tire.

items.label: Substantive use:
exampleLines: The [[u]]kind[[/u]] receive their rewards but the [[u]]unjust[[/u]] are often surprised.
(i.e. the kind person; the unjust person)

learn.title: Learn Greek Adjectives

content.text: Adjectives modify nouns and pronouns. They will match the nouns they modify in number, gender and case.

masculine = 2nd declension forms,
feminine = 1st declension forms, and
neuter = 2nd declension forms.
When an adjective's root ends in an epsilon, iota, or rho, the "a" 1st declension form will be used.
for words ending in ε, ι, or ρ

rows.greek: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός

rows.gloss: you appear to men to be [[u]]righteous[[/u]]

content.text: The substantive use of the adjective is when the adjective is used as a noun. The substantive use often has the article.

rows.greek: οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον
Ὁ δὲ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται
rows.gloss: and the [[u]]righteous[[/u]] will live by faith

content.text: Sometimes neither the adjective nor the noun has the article in which case context must determine whether to translate it attributively or predicatively.

content.text: εἰμί is a stative verb (it indicates a state of being) and so has no voice (active, middle, passive).

In English "is" takes a [[u]]predicate nominative[[/u]] rather than the normal accusative. It is correct to say "This is he" and incorrect to say "This is him." Similarly in Greek a noun or pronoun in the nominative follows the verb εἰμί.

items: all forms except the second singular are enclitic often taking no accent; and
the third singular and plural may take a moveable ν

rows.greek: Ἠλίας εἶ; καὶ λέγει, Οὐκ εἰμί. Ὁ προφήτης εἶ σύ;
rows.gloss: Are you Elijah? and he said, "I am not." Are you the prophet?

topics.title: οὐ, οὐκ and οὐχ

content.text: οὐ is placed before the word it negates which is usually the verb. There are three forms of this word depending on the initial letter of the word that follows it:

content.condition: when before a word that begins with a consonant

examples.gloss: and you do not understand these things?
and you do not accept me

items.text: οὐκ before a vowel with a smooth breathing mark; and

content.condition: when before a vowel with a smooth breathing mark

examples.greek: καὶ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ἐν ὑμῖν
examples.gloss: and you do not have his word in you

items.text: οὐχ before a vowel with a rough breathing mark.

content.condition: when before a vowel with a rough breathing mark

examples.greek: καὶ οὐχ ὁ ἄνθρωπος διὰ τὸ σάββατον
examples.gloss: and not man for the sabbath
